title: Track Conversations Before Sales Growth
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece argues that the best sales-driven organizations measure conversation quality and quantity before they measure revenue, because nothing else happens without that first conversation. The author contrasts two mindsets: one that puts the product or service center stage and measures itself by revenue and market share, and another that puts the sales conversation itself center stage and measures quality meetings and demonstrations. The piece argues the second mindset is what top sales performers actually prioritize, investing more in conversational skill-building than in product messaging alone. It closes by asking readers directly what their own organization actually measures as its primary success metric.
points: Top sales performers prioritize conversation quality and quantity over product-focused metrics.
One mindset centers the product and measures revenue; the other centers the conversation itself.
Investing in conversational skills is what expands initial conversations into meaningful sales dialogue.
Measuring quality conversations teaches the whole team what actually drives revenue growth.
quotes: The organization depends on this team to grow the enterprise by adding new clients, patrons, students, or customers through the power of persuasion.
Those who have mastered the sales process have a somewhat different view and priority. They believe it is sales conversation, whatever form it takes, that belongs in lights.
When leaders and sales teams make the number of quality conversations, meetings, demonstrations, and presentations the primary goal, sales soon soar.
Sustaining an enterprise requires a team of people who promote, position, or sell the product or service.
Some organizations employ sales teams, while others rely on a marketing, public relations, or a customer relationship unit to promote and persuade.
The names and titles may vary, but the focus of their work is the same.
Examine the sales team at your organization and you will likely find a group of highly skilled and talented communicators who enjoy people and believe deeply in the enterprise.
They are constantly selling the benefits of doing more with what the organization does.
